f4b4bb981e:02f6bd1aa1bfc938.summary: Atlas Garden is an independent editorial platform exploring contemporary gardens, landscapes, and outdoor objects. f4b4bb981e:f4219e26c2845ba2.title: El Capricho de Gaudí
f4b4bb981e:f4219e26c2845ba2.summary: El Capricho, also known as Villa Quijano, is one of the few buildings Antoni Gaudí completed outside Catalonia. Built in Comillas between 1883 and 1885 for Máximo Díaz de Quijano, it is laid out to follow the sun from room to room, which earned it the nickname of the architectural sunflower. Today it is run as a cultural space that welcomes thousands of visitors a month, from families and school groups to international tourists. Its image had not kept pace with that role. The brand needed to work across tickets, signage, workshops, merchandise, digital channels and the building's 140th anniversary, and it had to do so without ever competing with the building it represents. The question was how to change the image of a Gaudí building, and who should be part of that decision.

f4b4bb981e:bac771e2414d976e.title: Local Local
f4b4bb981e:bac771e2414d976e.summary: Local Local is an urban inspiration hub with cultural consciousness. A remotely controllable space rooted in the local area. It's a café, an art gallery, a blank canvas, a portal to the depths of one's thouts, a transit point to everything. We seek breakthroughs within reality, and opportunities within those breakthroughs. Local Local cherishes every moment of pause, capturing instances that transcend daily routines, and preparing for future moments of sudden inspiration. The only limit here is the prohibition against stopping your imagination. It's a space for every free spirit to enjoy a relaxed lifestyle that is true to the present, inspiring the now, and can be enjoyed anytime, anywhere. We aim to create an urban inspiration capsule with a sense of city environment awareness and cultural consciousness.

f4b4bb981e:c51e5baede298a64.title: Città di Ancona
f4b4bb981e:c51e5baede298a64.summary: Ancona was born from geography: a promontory that bends into the sea, a natural feature that the ancients recognized and called "Ankón," the "elbow" of Italy. This singular curve, where the land embraces the sea, defines not only the morphology of the city, but also its cultural, economic, and symbolic identity. It is a shape that embodies both function and metaphor: shelter and openness, protection and horizon.

f4b4bb981e:d76ae412082ab5dc.summary: A 1985 Mercedes-Benz camper, known simply as the red car. I've driven it across Iceland and into the Highlands, through every kind of weather, using it as a base for traveling, photographing and scouting locations. These photographs turn the camera back on the vehicle itself, placing its familiar red shape in the landscapes I've been exploring. They document the journeys and stops along the way, from rough Highland tracks to quiet campsites.

f4b4bb981e:d0e1f30ecc70a48f.title: Instytut Adama Mickiewicza
f4b4bb981e:d0e1f30ecc70a48f.summary: The project, developed in collaboration with the Adam Mickiewicz Institute (IAM) team and the Culture.pl editorial team, aimed to build relationships with artists and creative communities (IAM visual identity) and present Polish culture and its creators to an international audience (Culture.pl). IAM works with artists and people in the cultural sector who think outside the box, experiment, challenge existing ideas and take risks. We wanted the Institute's visual identity to reflect this open and bold approach, while giving space to the work itself. Rather than compete with the artists' work for attention, the visual identity provides a clear, distinctive and flexible frame for presenting it.

f4b4bb981e:45a9357592e12b67.summary: Our experiences, assumptions, and emotions influence how we see the world. The same moment can hold different meanings depending on who is looking, where they stand, and what they bring with them.

f4b4bb981e:c911b390534d0537.title: Aether Scent
f4b4bb981e:c911b390534d0537.summary: A quiet bloom of botanical resonance, unfolding across seven living species. Aether Scent is a studio exploration of nature through a digital lens. An imagined collection of botanical essences in which every specimen moves between the familiar and the unknown, retaining traces of its organic origin while growing into something new.

f4b4bb981e:cd8abe45d7552823.title: Mascot Collection
f4b4bb981e:cd8abe45d7552823.summary: Meet Flowy, Glowy, and Peanut! Three little characters with their own personalities, looks, and stories. We had fun creating this collection and exploring different emotions, poses, and ways to bring these guys into apps, social media, and branding. Hope you enjoy them as much as we do!

f4b4bb981e:c460ad19d835a4f4.title: Noche en Blanco Málaga 2026
f4b4bb981e:c460ad19d835a4f4.summary: LNEB es un evento dedicado a la creación cultural en Málaga, que acoge actividades, exposiciones y propuestas artísticas abiertas al público. Esta edición se desarrolla bajo el lema "El futuro se escribe con música", una temática que toma la música como punto de partida para conectar cultura, innovación y participación ciudadana. Para su identidad visual nos hemos inspirado en el movimiento y la vibración del sonido. La propuesta se construye a partir de una tipografía variable y un sistema gráfico vivo, capaz de transformarse y reaccionar a la música. Las formas circulares que componen las letras hacen referencia a los ciclos lunares, conectando visualmente con el imaginario del evento. El sistema visual se expande mediante texturas, deformaciones y animaciones influenciadas por el Op Art, utilizando colores vibrantes y contrastados que refuerzan el carácter del evento. La identidad busca convertirse en una experiencia dinámica e interactiva.

f4b4bb981e:ec58974820919c94.title: TIDAL SCULPTURES ? Iceland
f4b4bb981e:ec58974820919c94.summary: Temporary sand islands in a lagoon on Iceland's east coast, shaped by wind, tides, and rain. Low evening light reveals sculptural ridges, dark textures, and cool blue water.

f4b4bb981e:a363c7135b5c591b.title: Farseer
f4b4bb981e:a363c7135b5c591b.summary: Farseer is a financial planning platform built around a spreadsheet interface, giving finance teams a familiar environment with high-performance technology underneath. The brand was built on the same principle. Spreadsheets became the foundation of the identity system, shaped into a visual language that feels lighter, faster, and more human than traditional finance software. When a product changes the way people work, it changes the way they feel about work too. We rebuilt Farseer across verbal identity, visual identity, motion, audio, sub-brands, and a new website.

f4b4bb981e:b3a821c5df2d9011.title: Tiempos inciertos
f4b4bb981e:b3a821c5df2d9011.summary: Visual identity and graphic communication system for Tiempos inciertos (Uncertain Times), the international congress organised by ADACE, the Spanish Association of Contemporary Art Directors, held at the Federico García Lorca Centre in Granada. The event reflects on the present and future of cultural institutions, addressing issues such as governance, collections, sustainability, new technologies and audiences. The graphic proposal builds on ADACE's distinctive yellow underline, a recurring element of its visual identity, expanding it into a vibrant palette inspired by text highlighters. The title Tiempos inciertos is partially obscured by the bands themselves, evoking a present marked by uncertainty, in which everything seems to be under review and in search of balance.

f4b4bb981e:61c3db0238d957c7.title: OTZ LAB
f4b4bb981e:61c3db0238d957c7.summary: OTZ LAB is OTEYZA's unisex fragrance collection. We designed the bottle, packaging and visual identity to translate the brand's dialogue between tradition and the avant-garde into perfumery. The bottle pairs the solidity of matte black steel with the fragility of glass, shaped like a test tube to evoke experimentation. A sphere in distinctive colours and textures identifies each fragrance, while the boxes feature compositions inspired by constructivism. A design that reinterprets traditional perfume packaging through structure, material and intention.

f4b4bb981e:8ff2934edd02d3de.title: Piega

The logo prints itself in reverse, the way wet ink does when you fold a page. Every garment keeps a red the street never sees: a lining, a hem tape, the back of a fold.

a4977d3fa4:faf2f2719a25cc9b.title: adidas and JD Go 109 Meters Above London With Rock Band Villanelle
a4977d3fa4:faf2f2719a25cc9b.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:faf2f2719a25cc9b.summary: Coming off the launch of “The Original,” a new campaign spotlighting adidas Originals’ staple apparel, JD recently reunited with Villanelle frontman Gene Gallagher for a special set in London’s Battersea Power Station. Hosted in collaboration with Elevator Music, the set built on the music platform’s signature format of inviting artists and DJs into elevators for an intimate performance. Though it typically takes place against metallic silver doors, this edition brought a new dimension to the setup, with Gallagher’s band performing against the London skyline in the venue’s historic Chimney Lift. For the show, Villanelle curated a setlist of popular hits including “Hinge,” “Some Chew Lip,” “Squeeze,” and “Placebo.” As they launched their grunge-rock sound up 109 meters, the band wore adidas Originals tracksuits. In line with the campaign’s celebration of self-expression and individuality, they styled the collection with T-shirts and sneakers that complemented their signature look.Following the performance, Villanelle will tour the UK, headlining shows in Glasgow, Manchester and London next month. Meanwhile, adidas looks ahead to hosting more gigs in unique locations as part of The Original (Live). With Spanish artist MDA featuring in the previous installment, it is expected to expand its portfolio by spotlighting artists from a diverse array of genres.You can take a look back at the exclusive set in the gallery above. To shop the adidas Originals at JD, head to the dedicated website now. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:1bb574ae6226ee6f.title: Apple Announces its Designers of Tomorrow for 2026
a4977d3fa4:1bb574ae6226ee6f.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:1bb574ae6226ee6f.summary: Apple has announced Parafernalia, Yoonjeong Lee, Salem S. Charabi and Isabel Rower as the four recipients of its "Designers of Tomorrow" award for 2026. The news was unveiled at an exhibition taking place during this year's Design Miami Paris, with new works by each of the four designers on view, each responding to the theme of "Design for Presence"."Each of the works invites you to look closer and engage in multiple senses," said juror member Jennifer Dunlop Fletcher, who is a curator at SFMOMA. "Instead of spectacle, each work beckons a one-on-one encounter to notice detail. These details bring the intimate experience of the work into a moment of focus and presence."For Parafernalia, a studio made up of designers Sebastián Zorrilla and Genki Matsumura (who are based between Monterrey and Mexico City respectively) the theme made them think about conviviality of presence, noting that it is "seldom a singular condition"This manifested in MonoAmbiente 1, a multifunctional piece that explores how different forms of presence – such as a conversation, or a game of chess – can coexist within a single object.Closed, they describe the unit as a "landscape" with acid-etched stainless steel surfaces. Inside, you find stools and a table and a chess board – one set of pieces made by Matsumura, and the other by Zorrilla. Egyptian Danish architect Salem S. Charabi turned to one of the oldest ways of drawing people together. “Light is something we’re all instinctively drawn to, dating back to our earliest fires,” he said, a thought that led him to the lantern.The result is The Eminence of Light. Its veil is made from banana paper, using Japanese techniques applied to Egyptian palm, and sits over a skeleton of hand-stacked date palm fronds on a grooved limestone base. Each strand is three millimetres wide, split by hand and drilled, with ends sharpened by chisel so they interlock. Brooklyn-based Isabel Rower is interested in what happens when an everyday object is made from…

a4977d3fa4:eae91f68e982ceb6.title: Roger Gastman on Why Visibility Doesn't Equal Longevity in Art
a4977d3fa4:eae91f68e982ceb6.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:eae91f68e982ceb6.summary: Summary 'State of Art' is a new HypeArt series inviting artists, curators, collectors and other leading voices to weigh in on the ideas, debates and cultural shifts shaping contemporary art. Through intimate questions and personal recommendations, the series offers a closer look at what is exciting the art world, what needs to change and where things may be heading next. Getting noticed has never been easier for artists. A single post can reach millions, independent exhibitions can attract collectors, and entire careers can take shape outside the traditional gallery system. But turning that attention into something lasting is another story.Few understand that distinction quite like Roger Gastman. The curator, filmmaker, and founder of BEYOND THE STREETS has spent decades championing artists from graffiti, skateboarding, punk, and other creative communities that built their own audiences long before receiving institutional recognition.For the latest installment of State of Art, Gastman reflects on what separates a moment of attention from a meaningful career. While social media has given artists more independence, he argues that visibility alone isn't enough. The relationships, infrastructure, and long-term thinking behind the work are just as important as the work itself.From the value of gallery representation to the importance of making something undeniable, Gastman offers a perspective on what artists should really be chasing."The important thing is that somebody is thinking beyond the next sale."Has social media changed the balance of power between artists and galleries?Absolutely. Artists used to need galleries, magazines, critics, museums and a handful of gatekeepers just to get their work seen or considered. Now an artist can make something in their studio in the morning and have a thousands of people looking at it that same afternoon. That’s incredible.But visibility and career aren’t necessarily the same thing. Social media is very good at creating…

a4977d3fa4:81d416ebb5098768.title: Announcing Hypebeast Magazine #38: The Juice Issue
a4977d3fa4:81d416ebb5098768.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:81d416ebb5098768.summary: It's been called sauce, swag, aura, and charisma, but none of those words quite do the job. Hypebeast Magazine #38: The Juice Issue is dedicated to Juice, the energy behind the artists, designers, and builders who move culture forward. Across 288 pages, we trace where Juice comes from and how it travels: from a beat uploaded in someone's bedroom, to a sold-out concert, to a creative director's moodboard.Buy HereThe issue arrives with three covers. Xaviersobased, New York's defining Gen Z rapper and producer, opens up to writer John Norris about protecting his independence, taking underground rap mainstream, and why caring about people matters more than playing the part. Yohji Yamamoto, who rarely gives interviews, speaks with Ashley Ogawa Clarke while preparing his SS27 womenswear show about music, his worries for the next generation of designers, and why he still starts every collection from zero. And Tite Kubo, creator of the infamous manga BLEACH, drew an exclusive, original illustration for his cover, and sits down with Ora Margolis to talk about 15 years of weekly deadlines and why the series still endures a decade after it concluded.Buy HereOn the music front, the issue features in-depth stories on Knocked Loose, Syd, and Cash Cobain, plus an exclusive China tour diary from Berlin techno-punk duo Brutalismus 3000.Fashion stories go inside Kei Ninomiya's debut DSM Kei Ninomiya runway show and spotlight LVMH Prize winner Soshi Otsuki, CFDA winner Melitta Baumeister, Taiwanese label Professor.E, Italian designer Mattias Gollin, and Jaden Smith's first menswear collection at Christian Louboutin.Art and design features dive into Raymond Pettibon's album cover art, Los Angeles portraitist Kohshin Finley, British maker-designer Max Lamb, and NYC lighting studio Vy Voi.Buy HereElsewhere, we profile Memphis Depay, the Netherlands' all-time top football scorer; talk with British author Gabriel Krauze about his novella celebrating the Nike Air Max 95; and meet Psyche…

a4977d3fa4:b3dd88854e20fc6c.title: Blauer’s New Season Collection Is Made for Winters in the City
a4977d3fa4:b3dd88854e20fc6c.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:b3dd88854e20fc6c.summary: This season, Blauer elevates its technical apparel to support active city lifestyles. As captured in its latest campaign, featuring UK music artists DYLAN, Cassyette, and Ben Kidson, the new collection aims to provide contemporary style without sacrificing core functionality.In contrast to last season’s rugged, outdoors-ready clothing, the Fall/Winter 2026 range takes on a sharper look throughout its four lines: B Department, B Essential, B Project, and B. Urban Police. A staple for the cooler months, the down jacket is reworked in new ways, including a casual wave-quilted jacket, a thermoregulating graphene version, and a unique semi-transparent ripstop piece with visible feathers. To accentuate the sleek aesthetic, the brand also delivers leather jackets in biker, pilot, and military-inspired cuts. The varied silhouettes adapt Blauer’s heritage styles with washed treatments and a versatile color palette of “Black Ink,” “London Fog,” “Total Eclipse,” and “Peat.” For much-needed winter layering, these jackets drop alongside ribbed jumpers and polo knits. Elsewhere, the new collection also features a special edition B.Cortina capsule. Designed more specifically for mountain escapes, the range offers thermal jackets and a coordinated outerwear set, both adorning a Queen of the Dolomites-inspired print. You can now check out the pieces in the new campaign lensed by Bryan Adams. Adopting Blauer’s signature black-and-white aesthetic, he frames the contemporary feel of the garments while highlighting the cast’s unmistakable individuality. Shop Blauer’s Fall/Winter 2026 collection on its website and at select stockists worldwide. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:ede4e74219890865.title: The Salomon XT-6 PROTECTIVE and XT-WHISPER GTX Receive BILLY’S-Exclusive Colorways
a4977d3fa4:ede4e74219890865.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:ede4e74219890865.summary: Name: Salomon XT-6 PROTECTIVE & XT-WHISPER GTX BILLY’s ExclusivesColorway: Stormy Weather/Dark Navy/Trooper, Grisaille/Dark Navy/BlackSKU: TBCMSRP: ¥26,400 - ¥29,700 JPY (approx. $167 - $188 USD)Release Date: October 23Where to Buy: BILLY’s TokyoSalomon continues to blur the lines between rugged outdoor performance and urban streetwear with a newly unveiled footwear capsule arriving exclusively at BILLY'S. The drop reimagines two of the French brand's most celebrated technical silhouettes - the XT-6 PROTECTIVE and the XT-WHISPER GORE-TEX - in mood-evoking, weather-ready colorways. Designed to adapt effortlessly to both city streets and unpredictable natural environments, the collection beautifully balances cutting-edge utility with a sophisticated.The XT-6 PROTECTIVE takes the darker, more utilitarian route, replacing the model’s usual technical mesh emphasis with a ripstop upper inspired by workwear. Its "Stormy Weather" base reads as a muted blue-grey, overlaid with pale Trooper green-grey SensiFit lines that trace the sidewalls and toe before giving way to Dark Navy and black around the heel and heavily lugged sole. The matte ripstop surface and tonal overlays give the shoe a more protective, uniform-like character, while black Quicklace cords and oversized Salomon branding add sharper contrast. a4977d3fa4:207e591ac72813b6.title: Marina Abramović Turns Eight Decades of Life Into ‘Long Life, Short Stories’
a4977d3fa4:207e591ac72813b6.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:207e591ac72813b6.summary: Summary Marina Abramović reflects on memory, creativity and personal philosophy in Long Life, Short Stories .The illustrated volume blends drawings, anecdotes and introspection.Published by Rizzoli Electa, the 224-page book is priced at $65 USD. Marina Abramović turns inward for Long Life, Short Stories, a new illustrated volume that reframes one of performance art’s most uncompromising careers through memories, drawings and personal reflection. The book unfolds as what its publisher, Rizzoli Electa, describes as part sketchbook, part diary and part personal philosophy, moving through subjects including love, sex, loss, fear, nature, ancestry, creativity, dreams and even love spells. The fragmented format feels particularly suited to an artist whose practice has long used lived experience as material, offering a more intimate counterpart to the endurance, vulnerability and physical risk that have defined her public work.Published as Abramović celebrates her 80th birthday in 2026, the book arrives at another significant point in a career that helped establish performance art as a major contemporary discipline. Since emerging in the early 1970s, the Serbia-born artist has repeatedly tested the physical and psychological boundaries between performer and audience, from early works including Rhythm 0 and Rhythm 5 to her landmark 2010 Museum of Modern Art retrospective The Artist Is Present. Long Life, Short Stories approaches that history from a deliberately different angle. Original drawings created for the publication sit alongside direct, often humorous accounts and philosophical observations, revealing some of the emotional and psychological terrain behind works more commonly discussed through ideas of endurance, time, presence and bodily limits.The book is less a chronological autobiography than a loosely assembled map of Abramović’s inner world, shifting between the mystical, provocative and unexpectedly everyday while allowing personal episodes to sit alongside…

a4977d3fa4:184b3f542c13ac4a.title: Paulin’s Mara Gets a Genuine Galvanic Gilt Dial for Hodinkee
a4977d3fa4:184b3f542c13ac4a.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:184b3f542c13ac4a.summary: Summary Paulin and Hodinkee rework the Mara with a vintage-inspired gilt dial and aged lume.The limited edition uses a slimmer 11.8mm case and Miyota 9039 automatic movement.Limited to 250 pieces, it is priced at $1,000 USD. Paulin and Hodinkee have teamed up on a limited edition of the Mara, revisiting the Glasgow watchmaker’s first dive watch through the lens of mid-century tool watches. Founded in 2013 and operating alongside sister brand anOrdain, Paulin has built its identity around expressive color, typography and playful modern design, but the Mara Limited Edition for Hodinkee takes a deliberately more archival direction. Its 39.7mm stainless-steel cushion case retains the architecture of the standard Mara, while the dial trades Paulin’s usual geometric markers for classic diver indices, warm gilt accents and antiqued Super-LumiNova inspired by the black-and-gold dive watches of the 1950s and early ’60s.The defining feature is its genuine galvanic gilt dial, produced using a traditional process rather than simply printing gold-colored details onto a black surface. Each brass dial is first electroplated in gold before the minute track, logos and lettering are masked with a chemical resist; a subsequent galvanic treatment turns the exposed areas matte black, leaving the underlying gold visible through the markings. Paulin then hand-paints the hour markers with aged-tone Super-LumiNova to match the hands and bezel scale. Other period-minded touches include the meters-first depth rating, a gilt Hodinkee signature at 4 o’clock and Paulin’s custom Wim typeface, while a dark grey 120-click bezel uses a double-domed sapphire insert. A black-and-grey striped NATO strap with a Hodinkee-signed buckle completes the vintage-informed treatment.Inside, the collaboration swaps the Swiss movement used by the standard production Mara for a Miyota 9039 automatic calibre, providing a 42-hour power reserve while helping slim the case from 13.5mm to 11.8mm. Water resistance has…

a4977d3fa4:2f11993f394e2c7e.title: Gwyneth Paltrow Lands First Lead Television Role in A24 Drama 'The Apology' at Netflix
a4977d3fa4:2f11993f394e2c7e.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:2f11993f394e2c7e.summary: Summary Gwyneth Paltrow is set to headline her first television series in A24’s upcoming drama 'The Apology'Netflix has issued a straight-to-series two-season commitment for the cold-case thrillerThe production comes amid an executive restructuring at Netflix spearheaded across its scripted divisions Netflix and A24 have officially greenlit a two-season order for The Apology, marking the first-ever lead television vehicle for Academy Award winner Gwyneth Paltrow. The thriller drama series pairs the independent entertainment company with acclaimed Danish filmmaker Thomas Vinterberg.Paltrow stars as Evelyn Amspoker, a grief-stricken mother whose son was murdered 18 years ago in a high-profile cold case. Per the series logline, “When a stranger suddenly appears and confesses, justice finally seems possible,” until Evelyn and her husband, Caleb, discover that the perpetrator may receive a reduced sentence. “Faced with that unbearable truth, Evelyn and Caleb decide to take matters into their own hands.”The drama is created, written, and showrun by Joe Murtagh (The Woman in the Wall), with Another Round director Thomas Vinterberg slated to direct. Joe Hipps of Cut To executive produces alongside Murtagh, Vinterberg, and Paltrow. a4977d3fa4:7b80e4a1fa5227af.title: Dan Lin Dismissed as Netflix Film Chief Amid Major Executive Restructuring
a4977d3fa4:7b80e4a1fa5227af.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:7b80e4a1fa5227af.summary: Summary Dan Lin has been dismissed as Netflix’s head of film after almost three years leading the divisionThe departure follows sweeping corporate layoffs of roughly 1,000 employees and the firing of chief content officer Bela BajariaFormer Warner Bros executives Mike De Luca and Pam Abdy are speculated to be in talks for roles at the studio as a successor is sought Netflix has officially dismissed its head of film, Dan Lin, after nearly three years leading the division. The executive departure comes in the midst of a sweeping corporate and creative restructuring across the streaming giant.Lin's dismissal follows a wave of approximately 1,000 layoffs at the streamer last week, which also saw the firing of chief content officer Bela Bajaria, as well as the exits of Lin’s right hand Doug Belgrad and indie film division head Sheroum Kim. Netflix has since brought in veteran film and television executive Peter Rice to replace Bajaria following engagement concerns and stock stagnation in the wake of the company's defeated bid for Warner Bros. Lin was let go at the start of the weekend and is slated to address his teams on Monday, following recent appearances at Saturday’s Academy Gala and a Sunday screening for La Bola Negra on the Netflix campus.A Netflix spokesperson offered no immediate comment on Lin's exit, and while an official replacement has not been announced, former Warner Bros. Motion Picture Group leaders Mike De Luca and Pam Abdy have been widely speculated to be discussing potential roles at the company. Lin originally transitioned to Netflix in 2024 to replace Scott Stuber after leading his production banner Rideback, known for the animated Lego franchise, It, and Sherlock Holmes. In a June interview with The New York Times, Lin revealed that he had greenlit or acquired 88 films during his tenure, citing standouts such as Apex, Emelia Perez, Here Comes the Flood and The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth. a4977d3fa4:741e74d082a27bbb.summary: Summary Elon Musk announced on X that he plans to give one SpaceX share to every child in the United States next yearThe proposed distribution would encompass roughly 72.1 million minors and exceed a total value of $10.5 billion USDThe allocation is slated to roll out via tax-deferred youth investment accounts introduced by the Treasury Department SpaceX chief Elon Musk has announced a plan to distribute one share of the aerospace company to every minor in the United States. The pledge was revealed via X early Monday, representing a potential giveaway valued at over $10.5 billion USD.Posting to X, Musk stated: “Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America. This will be the first of many.” According to U.S. Census Bureau data, roughly 21.1% of the country's 341.8 million residents are under the age of 18, representing approximately 72.1 million eligible youth. Musk maintains a 48.4% beneficial stake in SpaceX with roughly 6.42 billion shares, contributing to an estimated net worth of $908 billion USD.The stock distribution will reportedly be facilitated through Trump Accounts, the tax-deferred investment accounts for American citizens under 18 established by the Treasury Department in July. Musk's announcement followed an exchange regarding artificial intelligence rival Anthropic, which committed 5% of its shares to an internal public benefit fund. Musk responded directly to the news, commenting, “I recommend giving the shares directly to the public,” before adding, “This is what I will be doing.”SpaceX—which encompasses rocket operations, satellite internet, artificial intelligence, and social platform X—went public in June. After debuting at $150 USD per share and peaking at $225.64 USD, the stock is currently trading just under its initial listing price.Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America.This will be the first of many.— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) October 19, 2026 Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:2a3e327a5e418d7a.title: Jean Prouvé’s Antony Chair Returns in a Limited Vitra Edition

a4977d3fa4:2a3e327a5e418d7a.summary: Summary Vitra releases a 2026 limited-edition reissue of Jean Prouvé’s 1950s Antony chair.The design features a black European chestnut shell and powder-coated metal frame.Now available online, each exclusive chair includes a consecutively numbered label. Vitra revisits one of Jean Prouvé’s most recognizable furniture designs with a new limited edition of the Antony Chair, updating the early-1950s original through a darker, more graphic material palette.The edition pairs a black European chestnut seat shell with a deep black powder-coated metal frame, sharpening the chair’s distinctive silhouette while allowing the natural grain of the timber to soften its industrial character. The contrast between Prouvé’s engineered metal structure and the warmth of wood remains central to the design, preserving the tension between technical precision and material tactility that has long defined the Antony. Each example is finished with a consecutively numbered label, reinforcing its limited-edition status.The release also carries particular significance within Vitra’s own history. The Antony was the first Prouvé design acquired by Vitra Chairman Emeritus Rolf Fehlbaum, who encountered a vintage example in Paris in 1984; that discovery sparked a deeper interest in Prouvé’s work and ultimately helped establish Vitra’s long-running relationship with the designer’s family.By returning to the chair in this monochromatic 2026 edition, Vitra highlights both the enduring clarity of Prouvé’s construction and the design’s role in shaping the brand’s engagement with his archive. The Vitra Limited Edition Antony Chair 2026 is available now via Vitra’s website. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:9c857ff97b3a3e1d.summary: STAFFONLY has officially released its Spring/Summer 2027 collection, "No Duty to Be Cute." Using the daily routine of a zookeeper as a starting point, the collection draws a parallel between the selective domestication of animals based on human aesthetic standards and the identity discipline found in modern workplaces, exploring how individuals gradually lose their unique traits while adapting to societal rules.This season draws inspiration from zookeeper uniforms, reinterpreting daily workwear through deconstructed tailoring, twisted structures, and fabric treatments. Repeatedly rolled-up cuffs are transformed into wavy pleats and dense gathers, while the shirt placket, tie, and bodice break the rigid structure of traditional uniforms through asymmetrical design. Some pieces also incorporate moldable metal wire, laser cutting, and multi-layered collars and cuffs, simulating the deformation of clothing caused by long-term wear and external forces. Washed distressed finishes and abstract animal camouflage patterns further enrich the collection's visual layers.The runway show continued this theme, designed to simulate a workplace hiring casting. Models appeared sequentially with different gaits, completing turns, positioning, and other actions on command, gradually forming a unified behavioral pattern. Subsequently, the models changed into standardized professional uniforms and black-framed glasses, lying down in white positioning grids according to their numbers. When they finally left, only neatly arranged work boxes and identity tags remained, illustrating how individuals are shaped by institutionalized work roles.In addition, STAFFONLY teamed up with Corona this season to launch the "Workation" collaborative project. Inspired by the fully open-top can design, the collection features interactive T-shirts printed with hidden "OFF DUTY" text, paper straw pull-tab hats, portable flask bags, and luggage tags, integrating the concepts of clocking out and vacationing…

a4977d3fa4:29a23906fd284df6.summary: Summary Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts will miss the remainder of the season after doctors discovered blood clots in his lungsHurts is clinically stable and expected to make a full recovery following a minimum three-month treatment on anticoagulation medicationA joint statement from the Eagles and agent Nicole Lynn confirmed he will remain around the team while conditioning during his recovery Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts has been ruled out for the remainder of the NFL season after doctors discovered multiple blood clots in his lungs. The medical update was officially confirmed in a joint statement released Monday by the franchise and Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn.According to the statement, Hurts underwent further medical evaluation after initially being diagnosed with a superficial clot in his calf. The subsequent testing revealed "a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli." While the Pro Bowl passer is currently "clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations," league protocol and medical guidance prohibit him from taking part in contact football activities while prescribed anticoagulation medication.Treatment for the blood clots is slated to take at least three months, according to Rapoport, officially ending his 2026 campaign. Despite the stoppage, the organization and medical personnel expressed complete optimism regarding his return to the field. "Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery," the statement confirmed. "We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects."https://t.co/aInIuUYiQJ— Nicole Lynn (@AgentNicoleLynn) October 19, 2026 Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:7d3c716f1303f9da.title: Reference Festival Opens ‘Freie Kunst’ Edition in Paris
a4977d3fa4:7d3c716f1303f9da.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:7d3c716f1303f9da.summary: Summary REFERENCE FESTIVAL has launched a Paris edition, running from October 19 through 25 parallel to Art Basel ParisThemed “FREIE KUNST,” the program entails immersive installations, live performances, intimate discussions, and all-night music programming dedicated to porous creative practices and approaches The festival unfolds across four venues: Dover Street Market Paris, Reference Salon, Silencio, and Institut du Monde Arabe REFERENCE FESTIVAL first made major headlines as “Berlin’s 24-Hour Fashion Festival.” In the years since its first edition, the German festival has expanded into realms of art, music, and technology, serving as a biannual gathering for some of the most exciting voices in culture.The festival, run by PR agency Reference Studios, has touched down in France for its first-ever Paris edition, running alongside the ongoing Art Basel from October 22 to 25. Fair week means sorting through hundreds of events, shows, and afters around the city, but if a ritualistic live performance by Michele Lamy or a Fassbinder-inspired collection by GmbH is more your speed, consider adding REFERENCE to your calendar.Since launching in 2019, the festival has gained a global rep for its eclectic programming and embrace of experimental creative approaches. This year’s edition, titled “FREIE KUNST,” takes after the German phrase for “free art” or “fine art,” and takes the studio’s commitments to creative fluidity one step further.The 2026 festival features a stacked schedule of live installations, intimate discussions, film screenings, and club nights, bringing together voices across disciplines to “consider the conjunction of freedom and creativity today,” said Mumi Haïati, Reference’s founder. “This is what our studio has been about since day one, and now we are bringing the entire scope of our network together for this meeting of minds around the idea of radical and unhinged exchange of ideas.”The program unfolds across several locations — Dover Street Market…

a4977d3fa4:fa5d5c6fa3f6a7db.title: Anna Uddenberg Explores Corporate Control in 'White Noise'
a4977d3fa4:fa5d5c6fa3f6a7db.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:fa5d5c6fa3f6a7db.summary: Summary Anna Uddenberg transforms Telegraph Gallery into a sterile office environment for her first solo exhibition in the Czech Republic.Sculptural figures merge with Herman Miller chairs and desks, exploring how corporate spaces influence the body and everyday behavior.Curated by Samuel Staples, White Noise opens October 22 and runs through February 4, 2027. For Anna Uddenberg's latest exhibition, White Noise, the Berlin-based artist is turning Telegraph Gallery in Olomouc, Czech Republic, into a corporate environment where furniture and the human body become increasingly difficult to separate.Opening October 22, the exhibition marks Uddenberg's first solo presentation in the Czech Republic. Known for her unsettling sculptures that explore body culture, consumerism and the influence of technology, the Swedish-born artist takes aim at the everyday objects and spaces that quietly dictate how we move, sit and behave.Most of what we've seen come out of Uddenberg's studio practice, sculptural figures appear to grow through desks and chairs, becoming extensions of the very objects designed to support them. And what initially resembles a functional office gradually reveals something more uncomfortable, where ergonomics gives way to control and the body becomes another piece of corporate furniture. Uddenberg has spent much of her career examining the relationship between people and the objects they use, often drawing from fashion, technology, wellness culture and public interiors. Her sculptures push these familiar references into strange territory, questioning whether the things designed to make our lives easier might also be shaping our behavior in ways we barely notice.White Noise opens October 22, 2026, and runs through February 4, 2027, at Telegraph Gallery in Olomouc, Czech Republic.Telegraph GalleryJungmannova 3, 779 00Olomouc 9-HodolanyCzechia Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:be88c9e2ccd64fd6.title: McLaren Racing and PUMA Take Notes From James Hunt’s Rebellious Wardrobe for New Collection
a4977d3fa4:be88c9e2ccd64fd6.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:be88c9e2ccd64fd6.summary: For their latest collaboration, McLaren Racing and PUMA revisit racing’s golden era to craft a new collection honoring James Hunt. One of the most pioneering drivers at the time, Hunt’s legacy extends beyond the track with a rebellious personal style that still stands out today. The James Hunt collection was previewed last month at McLaren’s Designed to Race: Front Row runway show ahead of London Fashion Week. With racing drivers, music artists, and industry experts in attendance, the event highlighted the icon’s effortless dress sense through relaxed racing jackets, throw-over mid-layers, and graphic T-shirts. Combining cues from the film Rush and the nostalgic red-and-white scheme on Hunt’s car, the black racing jacket features striking piping and the driver’s signature on the collar. Elsewhere, T-shirts play on Hunt’s expressive approach to customizing his clothes with doodles and text. a4977d3fa4:63f84783f85288d8.title: Saint Laurent Spotlights Martin Parr's Playful Self-Portraits in Paris
a4977d3fa4:63f84783f85288d8.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:63f84783f85288d8.summary: Summary Saint Laurent Montaigne presents 'Autoportrait,' a selection of Martin Parr's self-portraits curated by Anthony Vaccarello.Taken between 1996 and 2015, the images capture Parr's playful take on tourism, identity and the quirks of everyday life.The exhibition pays tribute to the late British photographer and runs through January 13, 2027, in Paris. Saint Laurent is paying tribute to the late British photographer Martin Parr with Autoportrait, a new exhibition at its Montaigne location in Paris. Curated by creative director Anthony Vaccarello, the presentation brings together a selection of self-portraits taken between 1996 and 2015, offering a look at the photographer's signature humor from the other side of the lens.Best known for his colorful, often absurd observations of everyday life, Parr spent decades photographing everything from crowded beaches and tourist attractions to the peculiar habits of modern consumer culture. For Autoportrait, however, he became the subject himself, handing the camera over to professional photographers, local amateurs and photo booths during his travels around the world.The resulting images are anything but conventional. With kitschy backdrops, elaborate disguises and occasionally heavy-handed retouching, Parr poked fun at the familiar rituals of vacation photography. Works featured in the exhibition include portraits taken in Singapore in 2007 and London in 2008, each reflecting his fascination with how people choose to present themselves.The exhibition also builds on Parr's longstanding relationship with Saint Laurent, which previously tapped the photographer for its 2025 campaign, An Ordinary Day, under Vaccarello's creative direction.Parr, who passed away in December 2025 at the age of 73, remains one of the most recognizable figures in documentary photography. A longtime Magnum Photos member and former president of the agency, he leaves behind a body of work that made the ordinary feel strange, funny and, at times,…

a4977d3fa4:f17bd169817ae274.title: MODMNT Reworks Military Classics Into Modular Down Jackets
a4977d3fa4:f17bd169817ae274.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:f17bd169817ae274.summary: MODMNT, a brand developed by NANGA CO., LTD., one of Japan’s leading down manufacturers, has released the second delivery of its 2026 Fall/Winter collection. The lineup features four styles of down wear reinterpreting functional garments rooted in hunting, military, and other distinct eras and purposes, alongside additional fall/winter pieces.MODMNT takes its name from “Modulement,” a coined term combining “Module,” “Mode,” “Equipment,” and “Element.” This season’s theme, “Beautifully Unpredictable,” translates the free-form processes of layering, removing, adding, and rearranging into the designs, offering wear that transforms with how it’s styled.A standout piece in this delivery is the Field Down Jacket, a contemporary reconstruction of the classic hunting jacket. It features details such as a three-dimensional pocket that integrates a flap pocket with a hand warmer, along with leather patches at the shoulders. Beyond a detachable hood, the jacket incorporates a convertible structure that allows the hem’s skirt component to be extended, enabling the silhouette to change depending on how it’s worn. The outer shell uses a waterproof, breathable fabric with 11,000mm of water resistance and 8,500g/m²/24hr of breathability, filled with 180g of 760 fill-power Spanish duck down. It’s priced at ¥110,000 (tax included).The collection also includes the Super Mackinaw (¥99,000), based on the classic Mackinaw jacket and combining the waterproof, breathable fabric Aurora-Tex® with the flame-resistant material Hinok; the Aviator Jacket (¥93,500), based on a bomber jacket design and featuring multiple pockets; and the C-1 Vest (¥60,500), inspired by military radio vests.Combining elements from functional garments with distinct origins, MODMNT’s down wear allows wearers to transform their own style. The second delivery of the 2026 Fall/Winter collection is available now, having launched on Friday, October 16. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:18d02cdadf275834.title: Getting Ready for the Night Shift Is Like Clockwork for Naz Hassan
a4977d3fa4:18d02cdadf275834.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:18d02cdadf275834.summary: If there’s one process that signals the start of chef Naz Hassan’s night, it’s changing his shoes. Having worked in kitchens across Milan and now London, the simple act of swapping his lace-ups for a pair of work-ready clogs remains constant, helping him get physically and mentally into gear for a busy shift making Italian plates.Exploring what functionality in style means to the chef, Hypebeast heads to his acclaimed neighborhood restaurant, Ornella, for a new two-part UGG campaign. With the debut installment capturing stylist Joel Lyall moving through the night, the latest feature shows how Hassan adapts to the energy behind the counter, as well as the moment he winds down with the brand’s functional Fall 2026 offering. "During a busy day, we’re like an orchestra, and everyone needs to play their instrument in the best way."“Service starts when the first customer comes through the door,” Hassan explains, once he’s slipped into his chef whites and the UGG Otzo Western Clog. “What kicks in is that sense of duty: you have to perform because you’re selling goods that need to be served to the highest level it possibly can.” Today, the chef begins service by making risotto, one of his favorite dishes on the menu. “During a busy day, we’re like an orchestra, and everyone needs to play their instrument in the best way,” he shares. It's not just about the individual performance, though. Hassan mentions how, more importantly, they need to “stay in harmony” so the kitchen can run like clockwork. To keep him in top form, he is drawn to the silhouette’s contoured EVA footbed and lightweight rubber outsole for its support throughout the day. “Having a comfortable pair of shoes is non-negotiable because I’m standing on my feet for 16 hours,” he says. “Shoes are the only part of my uniform that can be personalized, so it's nice when I can bring a bit of myself to my work.”Though Hassan has over a decade of experience perfecting his routine to meet the demands of restaurants,…

a4977d3fa4:02950867285eb77a.title: Waymo Plans First Canadian Robotaxi Expansion in Toronto for 2028
a4977d3fa4:02950867285eb77a.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:02950867285eb77a.summary: Summary Alphabet subsidiary Waymo has announced plans to launch its driverless taxi service in Toronto by 2028Groundwork begins in the coming days with road mapping and software validation under Ontario's autonomous vehicle pilot programLocal partner Element Fleet Management will oversee all on-the-ground fleet maintenance charging and logistical operations Waymo has officially announced plans to launch its driverless robotaxi service in Toronto, marking the autonomous mobility company's first commercial expansion into Canada. The Alphabet subsidiary targets 2028 to transport its first public riders as technical groundwork begins across the city.Initial deployment kicks off in the coming days with high-definition street mapping and software training led by human specialists behind the wheel under Ontario's provincial autonomous pilot framework. Day-to-day operations—spanning vehicle maintenance, depot charging, and rider readiness—will be managed by Toronto-based partner Element Fleet Management, which currently oversees Waymo’s infrastructure in San Diego. "As a Canadian company, we are proud to be expanding our partnership with Waymo," stated Laura Dottori-Attanasio, chief executive of Element Fleet Management. Longtime backers CPP Investments and automotive parts manufacturer Magna also continue to support the company’s capital and vehicle assembly efforts.Waymo reports that its autonomous fleet has driven more than 400 million kilometers to date, yielding 95% fewer serious-injury collisions than human drivers. While the initiative has earned support from accessibility advocates such as CNIB for offering independent transportation, critics note that navigating heavy traffic and severe winter conditions will pose a rigorous test for the system. The Canadian rollout builds on Waymo's broader international roadmap alongside London and Tokyo.Waymo is scheduled to launch its driverless taxi service to riders in Toronto in 2028. d006da4fe3:26bb42beb62831bc.title: The China Price
d006da4fe3:26bb42beb62831bc.author: Zongyuan Zoe Liu
d006da4fe3:26bb42beb62831bc.summary: In 1971, as the international monetary system was on the brink of collapse, U.S. Treasury Secretary John Connally told a group of worried European finance ministers that the dollar was “our currency, but your problem.” The dollar had become that system’s official reserve currency in 1944, under the Bretton Woods agreement, making signatories subject to the whims of U.S. monetary policy. Even after Bretton Woods collapsed and many currencies floated freely, the dollar continued to dominate. In the last half century, U.S. currency power has only expanded, as more countries have integrated into the global economy and therefore grown to depend on the dollar. China, reliant on export-driven growth, is foremost among them.

d006da4fe3:22627d45ff3f3498.title: The Scramble for the Open Seas
d006da4fe3:22627d45ff3f3498.author: Michael Albertus
d006da4fe3:22627d45ff3f3498.summary: Over the last half millennium, societies around the globe competed to divide up the world’s land. Nearly every square inch of soil outside Antarctica is now owned and tucked within national borders. But the oceans have largely been spared that fate. There were times throughout history when countries tried to gate and regulate the seas, but they were too vast to be controlled for long periods. During the Cold War, as technology made it far easier to imagine partitioning the world’s waterways and seabeds, great powers avoided an unrestrained race to grab the oceans. Most governments agreed to deal with them through a patchwork of treaties and multilateral bodies that sought to guarantee freedom of navigation in international waters and assign coastal seabeds to adjacent littoral states.

d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.title: The Trouble With the Nuclear-AI Analogy
d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.author: Christopher LaRoche, Ankit Panda
d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.summary: In humanity’s quest to constrain the dangers from fast-advancing artificial intelligence, many have looked to the most revolutionary technology that preceded it: nuclear weapons. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has called artificial intelligence “far more dangerous than nukes.” Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who assigns The Making of the Atomic Bomb to employees and has likened himself to the Manhattan Project scientist Leo Szilard, describes the most powerful AI models as “weaponizable nuclear materials.” When asked how a technology such as AI can be regulated, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman often references the world’s nuclear materials watchdog, the International Atomic Energy Agency. Even the director of the CIA, John Ratcliffe, has made the same comparison.These comparisons capture real parallels. Like nuclear weapons, frontier AI is powerful and hard to control. Like nuclear technology, it can be used for good or for ill. And like the Cold War arms race, the race for AI breakthroughs may reorder the global balance of power. The nuclear analogy, then, seems to offer a blueprint for how to effectively govern a promising but potentially dangerous technology such as AI.

fc066e842d:ad406854d994c755.title: Ideas and Firm Dynamics When It Takes Two to Tango
fc066e842d:ad406854d994c755.author: Honghao Wang
fc066e842d:ad406854d994c755.summary: Teams of inventors now produce over 80 percent of U.S. patents, up from just 45 percent in 1976. Over the same period, inventor employment has become increasingly concentrated in large firms, rising six times more than overall employment concentration. To explain these trends, we develop a new model of endogenous team formation within firms and embed it in a general equilibrium model of the inventor labor market. Teams increase firms’ returns to scale by increasing the likelihood of productive matches between inventors. The value of these matches rises over time, possibly driven by increasing knowledge specialization. This causes large firms to expand and small firms to shrink in equilibrium, accounting for the observed increase in inventor employment concentration. Because firms do not internalize knowledge spillovers, there is misallocation of inventors across firms. The rise of team production amplifies this misallocation by a factor of six by reallocating inventors away from small firms that generate disproportionately large knowledge spillovers.

fc066e842d:49934de94c848c00.title: Relative Development and the Intelligence Divide: Human Capital, Technology Diffusion, and AI
fc066e842d:49934de94c848c00.author: Jonathan R. W. Temple
fc066e842d:49934de94c848c00.summary: Will artificial intelligence (AI) help poorer countries catch up? This paper argues that the answer depends less on access to AI than on the capacity to use new knowledge productively. We show that countries have narrowed gaps in capital and schooling more readily than gaps in productivity. Technology can diffuse widely without producing productivity convergence. Measured human capital explains only a modest share of productivity differences in levels, but is associated with sharply different mobility regimes. The estimated transition processes imply an expected time to exit the lowest-productivity state of about 65 years for economies below the estimated human-capital threshold, compared with about 25 years for those above it. This reconciles development accounting with the view of human capital as absorptive capacity. If AI mainly augments skilled workers and capable firms, it may reinforce existing gaps. If it lowers the costs of learning, adaptation, and implementation in weaker-capability economies, it could instead promote convergence. The Intelligence Divide is therefore not simply about access to AI, but about the capacity to turn knowledge into productivity.

fc066e842d:e0411ad22edea77d.title: Growth in Chains: EU Value Chain Productivity and its Slowdown
fc066e842d:e0411ad22edea77d.author: Lähdemäki, Sakari
fc066e842d:e0411ad22edea77d.summary: Abstract We study Europe’s post-2008 productivity slowdown using novel total factor productivity (TFP) measures that follow production beyond individual industries in global value chains (GVCs). We collect a newset of stylized facts: (1) the slowdown is broad-based, with productivity growth weakening both in final-producer industries and in upstream industries; (2) the staggered entry into force of bilateral investment treaties with China is followed by higher value-chain TFP and greater business-intangible investment; while (3) the gains associated with technology intangibles are weak. We use these facts to discipline a stylized two-region general-equilibrium model with business capabilities, technology-related knowledge, and cross-border knowledge spillovers. The calibration supports a two-stage interpretation of Europe’s experience: (1) sizeable initial integration gains because accumulated business capabilities convert market access into productivity, and (2) later losses when technology improvements are converted into productivity more effectively elsewhere.

fc066e842d:1aed792933eb29e0.title: A Fork in the Road for Global AI Governance: To Repair or Reconfigure Expert-Led Governance?
fc066e842d:1aed792933eb29e0.author: Olugbade, Olajide
fc066e842d:1aed792933eb29e0.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a live object of global governance, with expert-led institutional arrangements emerging across an international regime complex. While scholarship on epistemic communities and science-policy interfaces treats expertise as a mechanism for coordination under uncertainty, recent work in Objectual International Relations (O-IR) and Science and Technology Studies foregrounds knowledge politics, contested authority, and the co-productive character of governance. We bring these perspectives into conversation with AI governance through a reflexive workshop design using Nominal Group Technique, drawing on two expert workshops in the UK and US. Findings show that expert panels remain valued for structuring debate, coordinating knowledge, and lending legitimacy to policy action. Yet participants identified tensions around exclusion, elite and private capture, weak accountability, geopolitical constraints, and temporal misalignment between institutional processes and technological change. An object-centered analysis further shows that AI remains an unstable governance object; the knowledge required to govern it is contested and unevenly distributed; and expertise itself is politically charged and institutionally unsettled. We synthesize these tensions into two pathways: Repair and Reconfiguration. Repair seeks to stabilize AI as a governable object, standardize relevant knowledge, and secure expert authority through institutional continuity and procedural refinement. Reconfiguration seeks to keep AI contested, broaden credible forms of knowledge, and reshape expertise through participation, reflexivity, and engagement with politics. The framework provides a critical lens for assessing emerging institutional designs for global AI governance and the trade-offs they entail.

fc066e842d:cd03bbb2b7c0e7e7.title: From Individual to Social Imitation: How Communities Expand Organizational Search
fc066e842d:cd03bbb2b7c0e7e7.author: Christopher Tucci
fc066e842d:cd03bbb2b7c0e7e7.summary: Generative artificial intelligence illustrates a broader organizational puzzle: young, resource-constrained firms can build on knowledge produced across a wider field to address problems that exceed their internal experience. We theorize one mechanism as social imitation: a distributed and recursive process through which communities observe practices and outcomes across organizations, distill recurrent elements into portable strategies, circulate them, and revise the collective repertoire as adoption produces new evidence. This perspective endogenizes the object of imitation. Organizations do not merely copy practices; communities collectively produce what becomes available to copy. We distinguish the source of a candidate (directly observed organizations or a collective) from its mode of adoption (blind or informed), and examine four forms of imitation in an agent-based model of organizational search. Collective sourcing alone does not improve performance. Its value depends on situated evaluation: assessing whether a candidate fits the adopter's configuration. As interdependence increases, informed social imitation improves population performance and the best solution discovered. As problems grow, it becomes more likely to outperform informed imitation from one or several directly observed peers because collective distillation sustains a broader candidate repertoire. Most gains arise from evaluating a small candidate set, and population performance can improve when only a minority of organizations possesses evaluative capability. Social imitation thus reveals a division of cognitive labor: communities expand the strategies organizations can consider, while organizations create value by determining which strategies fit. It explains how firms can mobilize knowledge beyond their boundaries, and why widespread access to collective knowledge does not produce equal benefits.
